_how: Don's shorthand: say the name, the agent applies it in full. Source of truth: ~/.claude/templates/patterns.md ("patterns"); entries marked "shorthand" come only from the shorthand memory note. Where the two differed on 2026-10-15, patterns won; "checked" says what changed. Refresh this file whenever patterns.md changes.
checked: 2026-10-15 against patterns.md. Patterns won on: [always]/[for now] (the old "we currently…" and only-"never extractive" wording was retired 2026-10-12), three-line report (Status / Next / "say expand"), cheapest that works (always name a model; at most 2 builds at once), verified or not (name the check; a new check is first seen failing), record every ruling (on the Issue or PR and inline in the doc it governs).

items.name: research first
items.does: Before any new feature, idea or question: how established platforms handle this exact case, plus our past rulings. Never answer a new product question from memory.

items.name: well-worn
items.does: Name 2–3 precedents, pick the simplest that fits, build it and tell you what was chosen. Labelled Path: well-worn.

items.name: new territory
items.does: No clear precedent, they conflict, or it touches a ruling, legal, privacy, money or member trust: one A/B/C with a recommendation, before building.

items.name: adapt, don't adopt
items.does: A pattern made for human teams is a starting point: keep what still solves a problem, rebuild the rest for agents.

items.name: no speculative rulings
items.does: Rule only on what binds current work; prune the rest instead of asking you.

items.name: [always] / [for now]
items.does: Every never / won't / always ruling carries one: [always] = every version, [for now] = this version, reviewed at each release planning.

items.name: newer wins
items.does: When two recorded rulings conflict, the newer holds and work continues; only a chat remark that contradicts the record gets a one-line confirm.

items.name: one at a time
items.does: One decision or one page to review per message: the next one, the one that unblocks the most work soonest.

items.name: record every ruling
items.does: The moment you decide, write it on its Issue or PR and inline in the doc it governs; search that record before asking you anything.

items.name: save open threads
items.does: During a back-and-forth, save your words, where we got to and the next step after each substantive message.

items.name: do the mechanical work
items.does: Anything with no judgement (merges, env vars, Issues, labels, reruns, migrations while allowed) gets done, not handed to you.

items.name: Don directs, agents edit
items.does: You say what to change; agents change it. Never ask you to edit or paste into a file.

items.name: say it once
items.does: Name a real cost or collision once, plainly, then do what you asked.

items.name: what do I need to do
items.does: The answer lands in Your to-do at the top of this dashboard, each with priority 1–3, due by and/or what it unlocks, and comes off when done; also said in chat.

items.name: dashboard
items.does: This generated HTML page, with the sidebar. Markdown is only for short to medium text docs. (2026-10-15, replaces plan #146 B.)

items.name: three-line report
items.does: Status: Done / Blocked / Question, one sentence. Next: the ask, or none. Then "Want detail? Say expand."

items.name: copy-paste inline
items.does: Anything you will copy goes in the message as one code block, never a file or artifact.

items.name: phone / computer
items.does: phone (and office days): nothing needing a desktop approval or terminal; queue it. computer: everything.

items.name: safe to close
items.does: Every Code session ends with SAFE TO CLOSE or NOT SAFE TO CLOSE and why, so you know which sessions you can close.

items.name: no manual prompts
items.does: Tool-heavy work only in sessions that skip permission prompts; reuse a running session within the day.

items.name: cheapest that works
items.does: Least costly model, tool and plan that does the job: Haiku for status, Sonnet for routine and docs, Opus for design and tricky builds. Flag any new recurring cost first.

items.name: verified or not
items.does: Every "done" names the check that ran (live DB, local DB, unit tests only, or not verified); a new check is first seen failing.

items.name: earn the rule
items.does: A process change names the dated failure that earned it. No failure, no rule.

items.name: runs unattended
items.does: Every flow runs while you're away Tue–Thu; your items batch for Fri–Mon; one global switch over item-by-item controls.

items.name: self-correct first
items.does: Push a problem back to whoever can fix it before any staff work; escalate only on a repeat or a legal/safety must-have.

items.name: nothing gets lost
items.does: Everything you approved stays visible with its test; anything that disappears or loses its test is shown to you.

items.name: Now / Next / Considering / Later
items.does: The four fixed roadmap lanes: being built, settled and approved, possible, eventual.

items.name: Find / Discover
items.does: The tool side (search, businesslike) and the fun side (algorithmic, after beta).

items.name: agent vs human
items.does: Pick the reader first: you get what and why (PM doc), agents get how (agent doc). Never one doc for both.

items.name: PM doc
items.does: Bottom line first, a bold 1–3 line overview per section, the detail folded; fits one phone screen closed.

items.name: agent doc
items.does: One home per fact, current state plus why, a size budget, a check that proves it.

items.name: fewest docs
items.does: Never propose a new hand-kept doc; each kind of thing has one home; human views are generated.

items.name: current + why
items.does: Agent docs say what is true now and why, never the history; git is the history.
